   223→    /// Send text with chunking support.
   224→    async fn send_text_chunked(
   225→        &self,
   226→        account_id: &str,
   227→        to: &str,
   228→        text: &str,
   229→        reply_to: Option<&str>,
   230→        chunk_limit: usize,
   231→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   232→        let limit = if chunk_limit == 0 {
   233→            DEFAULT_CHUNK_LIMIT
   234→        } else {
   235→            chunk_limit
   236→        };
   237→        let chunks = chunking::chunk_message(text, limit);
   238→
   239→        for chunk in chunks {
   240→            let mut payload = serde_json::json!({
   241→                "type": "message",
   242→                "text": chunk,
   243→            });
   244→            if let Some(reply_to) = reply_to
   245→                && let Some(obj) = payload.as_object_mut()
   246→            {
   247→                obj.insert(
   248→                    "replyToId".into(),
   249→                    serde_json::Value::String(reply_to.to_string()),
   250→                );
   251→            }
   252→            self.send_activity_with_retry(account_id, to, payload)
   253→                .await?;
   254→        }
   255→        Ok(())
   256→    }
   257→
   258→    /// Edit-in-place streaming: post, then edit as tokens arrive.
   259→    async fn send_stream_edit_in_place(
   260→        &self,
   261→        account_id: &str,
   262→        to: &str,
   263→        reply_to: Option<&str>,
   264→        mut stream: StreamReceiver,
   265→        throttle: std::time::Duration,
   266→        chunk_limit: usize,
   267→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   268→        let mut session = StreamSession::new(throttle);
   269→
   270→        loop {
   271→            let event = tokio::select! {
   272→                event = stream.recv() => event,
   273→            };
   274→
   275→            match event {
   276→                Some(StreamEvent::Delta(delta)) => {
   277→                    session.push_delta(&delta);
   278→
   279→                    if session.ready_for_initial_post() {
   280→                        let activity = streaming::build_initial_activity(
   281→                            &session.text_with_suffix(),
   282→                            reply_to,
   283→                        );
   284→                        match self
   285→                            .send_activity_with_retry(account_id, to, activity)
   286→                            .await
   287→                        {
   288→                            Ok(outcome) => {
   289→                                if let Some(id) = outcome.activity_id {
   290→                                    session.set_activity_id(id);
   291→                                }
   292→                            },
   293→                            Err(e) => {
   294→                                warn!(account_id, to, "Teams stream initial post failed: {e}");
   295→                                // Fall through — will send final text when done.
   296→                            },
   297→                        }
   298→                    } else if session.ready_for_edit()
   299→                        && let Some(aid) = session.activity_id()
   300→                    {
   301→                        let update =
   302→                            streaming::build_update_activity(aid, &session.text_with_suffix());
   303→                        let _ = self.update_activity(account_id, to, aid, update).await;
   304→                        session.mark_edited();
   305→                    }
   306→                },
   307→                Some(StreamEvent::Error(err)) => {
   308→                    if !session.has_text() {
   309→                        session.push_delta(&err);
   310→                    }
   311→                    break;
   312→                },
   313→                Some(StreamEvent::Done) | None => break,
   314→            }
   315→        }
   316→
   317→        session.finalize();
   318→
   319→        if !session.has_text() {
   320→            return Ok(());
   321→        }
   322→
   323→        let final_text = session.final_text();
   324→
   325→        // If we posted an initial message, do a final edit.
   326→        if let Some(aid) = session.activity_id() {
   327→            let update = streaming::build_update_activity(aid, final_text);
   328→            let _ = self.update_activity(account_id, to, aid, update).await;
   329→        } else {
   330→            // Never posted — send the full text as a regular message.
   331→            self.send_text_chunked(account_id, to, final_text, reply_to, chunk_limit)
   332→                .await?;
   333→        }
   334→
   335→        Ok(())
   336→    }
   337→}

   339→#[async_trait]
   340→impl ChannelOutbound for MsTeamsOutbound {
   341→    async fn send_text(
   342→        &self,
   343→        account_id: &str,
   344→        to: &str,
   345→        text: &str,
   346→        reply_to: Option<&str>,
   347→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   348→        let chunk_limit = {
   349→            let accounts = self.accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   350→            accounts
   351→                .get(account_id)
   352→                .map(|s| s.config.text_chunk_limit)
   353→                .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_CHUNK_LIMIT)
   354→        };
   355→        self.send_text_chunked(account_id, to, text, reply_to, chunk_limit)
   356→            .await

   358→
   359→    async fn send_media(
   360→        &self,
   361→        account_id: &str,
   362→        to: &str,
   363→        payload: &ReplyPayload,
   364→        reply_to: Option<&str>,
   365→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   366→        if let Some(media) = payload.media.as_ref() {
   367→            if media.url.starts_with("data:") {
   368→                // Parse data URL and send as inline attachment.
   369→                if let Some(rest) = media.url.strip_prefix("data:")
   370→                    && let Some((header, b64_data)) = rest.split_once(",")
   371→                {
   372→                    let media_type = header.split(';').next().unwrap_or("image/png");
   373→                    if crate::attachments::is_inline_image(media_type)
   374→                        && let Ok(data) = base64::Engine::decode(
   375→                            &base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD,
   376→                            b64_data,
   377→                        )
   378→                    {
   379→                        let activity = crate::attachments::build_media_activity(
   380→                            &payload.text,
   381→                            &data,
   382→                            media_type,
   383→                            reply_to,
   384→                        );
   385→                        self.send_activity_with_retry(account_id, to, activity)
   386→                            .await?;
   387→                        return Ok(());
   388→                    }
   389→                }
   390→                // Fall back to text if data URL parsing fails.
   391→                let mut text = payload.text.clone();
   392→                if !text.is_empty() {
   393→                    text.push_str("\n\n");
   394→                }
   395→                text.push_str("[media: image attached]");
   396→                return self.send_text(account_id, to, &text, reply_to).await;
   397→            }
   398→
   399→            // External URL — send as URL attachment.
   400→            let mut activity = serde_json::json!({
   401→                "type": "message",
   402→                "attachments": [
   403→                    crate::attachments::build_url_attachment(
   404→                        &media.url,
   405→                        &media.mime_type,
   406→                        media.filename.as_deref(),
   407→                    )
   408→                ],
   409→            });
   410→            if !payload.text.is_empty() {
   411→                activity["text"] = serde_json::Value::String(payload.text.clone());
   412→            }
   413→            if let Some(reply_id) = reply_to {
   414→                activity["replyToId"] = serde_json::Value::String(reply_id.to_string());
   415→            }
   416→            self.send_activity_with_retry(account_id, to, activity)
   417→                .await?;
   418→            return Ok(());
   419→        }
   420→
   421→        // No media, just text.
   422→        self.send_text(account_id, to, &payload.text, reply_to)
   423→            .await
   424→    }

   478→    async fn send_interactive(
   479→        &self,
   480→        account_id: &str,
   481→        to: &str,
   482→        message: &moltis_channels::InteractiveMessage,
   483→        reply_to: Option<&str>,
   484→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   485→        // Build an Adaptive Card with action buttons.
   486→        let mut body: Vec<serde_json::Value> = vec![serde_json::json!({
   487→            "type": "TextBlock",
   488→            "text": message.text,
   489→            "wrap": true,
   490→        })];
   491→
   492→        for row in &message.button_rows {
   493→            let actions: Vec<serde_json::Value> = row
   494→                .iter()
   495→                .map(|btn| {
   496→                    serde_json::json!({
   497→                        "type": "Action.Submit",
   498→                        "title": btn.label,
   499→                        "data": {
   500→                            "msteams": { "type": "imBack", "value": &btn.callback_data },
   501→                        },
   502→                    })
   503→                })
   504→                .collect();
   505→            body.push(serde_json::json!({
   506→                "type": "ActionSet",
   507→                "actions": actions,
   508→            }));
   509→        }
   510→
   511→        let card = serde_json::json!({
   512→            "type": "AdaptiveCard",
   513→            "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json",
   514→            "version": "1.4",
   515→            "body": body,
   516→        });
   517→
   518→        let activity = crate::cards::card_activity(card, Some(&message.text));
   519→        if let Some(reply_id) = reply_to {
   520→            let mut a = activity;
   521→            a["replyToId"] = serde_json::Value::String(reply_id.to_string());
   522→            self.send_activity_with_retry(account_id, to, a).await?;
   523→        } else {
   524→            self.send_activity_with_retry(account_id, to, activity)
   525→                .await?;
   526→        }
   527→        Ok(())
   528→    }
   529→
   530→    async fn add_reaction(
   531→        &self,
   532→        account_id: &str,
   533→        channel_id: &str,
   534→        message_id: &str,
   535→        emoji: &str,
   536→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   537→        let (http, config, token_cache) = {
   538→            let accounts = self.accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   539→            let state = accounts
   540→                .get(account_id)
   541→                .ok_or_else(|| ChannelError::unknown_account(account_id))?;

   549→        let token=[REDACTED](&http, &config, &token_cache)

   552→
   553→        crate::graph::add_reaction(&http, &token, channel_id, message_id, emoji)
   554→            .await

   556→                ChannelError::external("Teams add reaction", std::io::Error::other(e.to_string()))
   557→            })
   558→    }

   572→            (

   582→
   583→        crate::graph::remove_reaction(&http, &token, channel_id, message_id, emoji)
   584→            .await
   585→            .map_err(|e| {

   593→
   594→#[async_trait]
   595→impl ChannelStreamOutbound for MsTeamsOutbound {
   596→    async fn send_stream(
   597→        &self,
   598→        account_id: &str,
   599→        to: &str,
   600→        reply_to: Option<&str>,
   601→        mut stream: StreamReceiver,
   602→    ) -> ChannelResult<()> {
   603→        let (stream_mode, throttle, chunk_limit) = {
   604→            let accounts = self.accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   605→            match accounts.get(account_id) {
   606→                Some(state) => (
   607→                    state.config.stream_mode.clone(),
   608→                    std::time::Duration::from_millis(state.config.edit_throttle_ms),
   609→                    state.config.text_chunk_limit,
   610→                ),
   611→                None => (
   612→                    StreamMode::Off,
   613→                    streaming::DEFAULT_EDIT_THROTTLE,
   614→                    DEFAULT_CHUNK_LIMIT,
   615→                ),
   616→            }
   617→        };
   618→
   619→        match stream_mode {
   620→            StreamMode::EditInPlace => {
   621→                self.send_stream_edit_in_place(
   622→                    account_id,
   623→                    to,
   624→                    reply_to,
   625→                    stream,
   626→                    throttle,
   627→                    chunk_limit,
   628→                )
   629→                .await
   630→            },
   631→            StreamMode::Off => {
   632→                // Accumulate and send once (original behaviour).
   633→                let mut text = String::new();
   634→                while let Some(event) = stream.recv().await {
   635→                    match event {
   636→                        StreamEvent::Delta(delta) => text.push_str(&delta),
   637→                        StreamEvent::Done => break,
   638→                        StreamEvent::Error(err) => {
   639→                            debug!(account_id, chat_id = to, "Teams stream error: {err}");
   640→                            if text.is_empty() {
   641→                                text = err;
   642→                            }
   643→                            break;
   644→                        },
   645→                    }
   646→                }
   647→                if text.is_empty() {
   648→                    return Ok(());
   649→                }
   650→                self.send_text_chunked(account_id, to, &text, reply_to, chunk_limit)
   651→                    .await
   652→            },
   653→        }
   654→    }
   655→
   656→    async fn is_stream_enabled(&self, account_id: &str) -> bool {
   657→        let accounts = self.accounts.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
   658→        accounts
   659→            .get(account_id)
   660→            .is_some_and(|s| s.config.stream_mode == StreamMode::EditInPlace)
   661→    }
   662→}
   663→

Everything clean. Here's what was added in this second pass:

## Additional Changes

### Graph API operations added to `graph.rs`:
- **`get_message()`** — fetch a single message by ID
- **`search_messages()`** — full-text search with OData `$search`, optional sender filter, `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` header, OData injection protection
- **`get_member_info()`** — fetch user profile (displayName, mail, jobTitle, userPrincipalName, officeLocation)
- **`pin_message()`** — pin a message, returns pinned-message resource ID
- **`unpin_message()`** — unpin using the pinned-message resource ID (not message ID)
- **`list_pins()`** — list all pins with `$expand=message`

### New data structures:
- `SearchResult` — search results container
- `MemberInfo` — user profile fields
- `PinnedMessage` — pinned message with distinct `pinned_message_id` vs `message_id`

### Outbound methods added:
- **`send_card()`** — send arbitrary Adaptive Cards
- **`edit_message()`** — edit an existing message by activity ID
- **`delete_activity()`** — delete an existing message by activity ID

### Default channels:
- `msteams` added to the default `offered` channels list in `ChannelsConfig`, so it appears in the web UI out of the box

### Test results:
- 70 msteams tests, 172 config tests, 76 channels tests — all pass
- Clippy clean, format clean, full workspace compiles

## Summary: Channel Onboarding Flow and Web UI Architecture

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete picture of how channels are onboarded in Moltis:

### 1. KEY WEB UI FILES

#### Main Assets
- **`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/web/src/assets/onboarding.html`** - Onboarding page template (renders to `#onboardingRoot`)
- **`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/web/src/templates/index.html`** - Main app template (renders to `#pageContent`)

#### Page Scripts
- **`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/web/src/assets/js/page-channels.js`** - Channels management page (17358 lines) - handles channels list, modals for Telegram/Teams/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp, senders approval
- **`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/web/src/assets/js/onboarding-view.js`** - Onboarding wizard (handles Auth, Identity, Provider, Voice, Channel, Summary steps)
- **`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/web/src/assets/js/page-onboarding.js`** - Page router for onboarding
- **`/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/web/src/assets/js/channel-utils.js`** - Shared channel utilities

### 2. CHANNEL RPC API METHODS

All implemented in `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/gateway/src/methods/services.rs`:

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `channels.status` | Fetch all configured channels (returns `{ channels: [] }`) |
| `channels.list` | Alias for `channels.status` |
| `channels.add` | Add a new channel: `{ type, account_id, config }` |
| `channels.remove` | Remove channel: `{ type, account_id }` |
| `channels.update` | Update channel config: `{ type, account_id, config }` |
| `channels.senders.list` | List senders/users for a channel account |
| `channels.senders.approve` | Approve a sender for DM access |
| `channels.senders.deny` | Deny a sender for DM access |
| `channels.logout` | Logout from a channel |

### 12. INITIALIZATION & LIFECYCLE

**Onboarding Page (`onboarding-view.js`):**
1. `ensureWsConnected()` - Starts WebSocket for events
2. Steps: Auth → Identity → Provider → Voice → Channel → Summary
3. `ChannelStep` calls `addChannel()` via RPC
4. On success, stores channel and advances to summary
5. Final "Complete" triggers redirect to main app

**Channels Page (`page-channels.js`):**
1. `initChannels(container)` - Mount to `#pageContent`
2. `loadChannels()` - Fetch via `channels.status` RPC
3. `loadSenders()` - Fetch senders for selected account
4. `onEvent("channel", handler)` - Listen for real-time updates
5. `teardownChannels()` - Cleanup on unmount

---

This architecture demonstrates a clean separation: **RPC methods** handle backend operations, **REST endpoints** receive platform webhooks, **Preact components** manage UI state via signals, and **WebSocket events** push real-time updates to the frontend.

### 3. **Config Template** (`crates/config/src/template.rs`, lines 628-648)
The Teams configuration example shows:
```toml
[channels.msteams.my-bot]
app_id = "..."                  # Azure Bot App ID
app_password = "..."            # Azure Bot App Password (client secret)
tenant_id = "botframework.com"  # Azure AD tenant ID (for JWT validation)
webhook_secret = "..."          # Optional query secret for webhook URL (?secret=...)
allowlist = []                  # User IDs allowed to DM (empty = all unless dm_policy=allowlist)
dm_policy = "allowlist"         # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
group_policy = "open"           # "open", "allowlist", or "disabled"
mention_mode = "mention"        # "mention", "always", or "none"
stream_mode = "edit_in_place"   # "edit_in_place" or "off"
edit_throttle_ms = 1500         # Min ms between streaming edits
text_chunk_limit = 4000         # Max chars per message chunk
reply_style = "top_level"       # "top_level" or "thread"
welcome_card = true             # Show welcome card in DMs
group_welcome_card = false      # Show welcome text in group chats
bot_name = "Moltis"             # Bot display name for welcome cards
prompt_starters = []            # Prompt starter buttons on welcome card
max_retries = 3                 # Max retry attempts for failed sends
history_limit = 50              # Max messages for thread context (Graph API)
```

### 4. **Teams-Specific Configuration** (`crates/msteams/src/config.rs`)
Full struct definitions show:
- **Authentication**: `app_id` (Azure Bot App ID), `app_password` (Secret<String>), `tenant_id`, `oauth_tenant`, `oauth_scope`
- **Access Control**: `dm_policy`, `group_policy`, `mention_mode`, `allowlist`, `group_allowlist`
- **Webhook Security**: `webhook_secret` (optional)
- **Streaming**: `stream_mode` (EditInPlace or Off), `edit_throttle_ms` (default: 1500ms)
- **Chunking**: `text_chunk_limit` (default: 4000 chars per message)
- **Welcome Cards**: `welcome_card` (default: true), `group_welcome_card`, `bot_name`, `prompt_starters`
- **Threading**: `reply_style` (TopLevel or Thread)
- **Retry Logic**: `max_retries` (default: 3), `retry_base_delay_ms` (250), `retry_max_delay_ms` (10000)
- **Graph API**: `graph_tenant_id`, `history_limit` (default: 50 messages)
- **Per-Team Overrides**: `teams` HashMap with TeamConfig entries (mention_mode, reply_style, per-channel overrides)
- **Model Selection**: `model`, `model_provider`, per-team/per-channel overrides

### 5. **CLI Bootstrap Command** (`crates/cli/src/channel_commands.rs`)
Location: `/Users/penso/.superset/worktrees/moltis/glistening-amazonsaurus/crates/cli/src/channel_commands.rs`

The `moltis channels teams bootstrap` command:
- **Args**: `account_id`, `app_id`, `app_password`, `base_url`, `webhook_secret`, `oauth_tenant`, `oauth_scope`, `force`, `dry_run`, `open`
- **Workflow**: 
  1. Prompts for account ID, app ID, app password, base URL
  2. Generates or accepts a webhook secret
  3. Builds webhook endpoint URL: `/api/channels/msteams/{account_id}/webhook?secret={secret}`

     1→# Channels
     2→
     3→Moltis connects to messaging platforms through **channels**. Each channel type
     4→has a distinct inbound mode, determining how it receives messages, and a set of
     5→capabilities that control what features are available.
     6→
     7→## Supported Channels
     8→
     9→| Channel | Inbound Mode | Public URL Required | Key Capabilities |
    10→|---------|-------------|--------------------|--------------------|
    11→| Telegram | Polling | No | Streaming, voice ingest, reactions, OTP, location |
    12→| Discord | Gateway (WebSocket) | No | Streaming, interactive messages, threads, reactions |
    13→| Microsoft Teams | Webhook | Yes | Streaming, interactive messages, threads |
    14→| WhatsApp | Gateway (WebSocket) | No | Streaming, voice ingest, OTP, pairing, location |
    15→| Slack | Socket Mode | No | Streaming, interactive messages, threads, reactions |
    16→
    17→## Inbound Modes
    18→
    19→### Polling
    20→
    21→The bot periodically fetches new messages from the platform API. No public URL
    22→or open port is needed. Used by Telegram.
    23→
    24→### Gateway / WebSocket
    25→
    26→The bot opens a persistent outbound WebSocket connection to the platform and
    27→receives events in real time. No public URL needed. Used by Discord and
    28→WhatsApp.
    29→
    30→### Socket Mode
    31→
    32→Similar to a gateway connection, but uses the platform's Socket Mode protocol.
    33→No public URL needed. Used by Slack.
    34→
    35→### Webhook
    36→
    37→The platform sends HTTP POST requests to a publicly reachable endpoint on your
    38→server. You must configure the messaging endpoint URL in the platform's
    39→settings. Used by Microsoft Teams.
    40→
    41→### None (Send-Only)
    42→
    43→For channels that only send outbound messages and do not receive inbound
    44→traffic. No channels currently use this mode, but it is available for future
    45→integrations (e.g. email, SMS).
    46→
    47→## Capabilities Reference
    48→
    49→| Capability | Description |
    50→|-----------|-------------|
    51→| `supports_outbound` | Can send messages to users |
    52→| `supports_streaming` | Can stream partial responses (typing/editing) |
    53→| `supports_interactive` | Can send interactive components (buttons, menus) |
    54→| `supports_threads` | Can reply in threads |
    55→| `supports_voice_ingest` | Can receive and transcribe voice messages |
    56→| `supports_pairing` | Requires device pairing (QR code) |
    57→| `supports_otp` | Supports OTP-based sender approval |
    58→| `supports_reactions` | Can add/remove emoji reactions |
    59→| `supports_location` | Can receive and process location data |
    60→
    61→## Setup
    62→
    63→Each channel is configured in `moltis.toml` under `[channels]`:
    64→
    65→```toml
    66→[channels.telegram.my_bot]
    67→token = "123456:ABC-DEF..."
    68→dm_policy = "allowlist"
    69→allowlist = ["alice", "bob"]
    70→
    71→[channels.msteams.my_teams_bot]
    72→app_id = "..."
    73→app_password = "..."
    74→
    75→[channels.discord.my_discord_bot]
    76→token = "..."
    77→
    78→[channels.slack.my_slack_bot]
    79→bot_token = "xoxb-..."
    80→app_token = "xapp-..."
    81→
    82→[channels.whatsapp.my_wa]
    83→dm_policy = "open"
    84→```
    85→
    86→For detailed configuration, see the per-channel pages:
    87→[Telegram](telegram.md), [Discord](discord.md), [Slack](slack.md),
    88→[WhatsApp](whatsapp.md).
    89→
    90→You can also use the web UI's **Channels** tab for guided setup with each platform.
    91→
    92→## Proactive Outbound Messaging
    93→
    94→Agents are not limited to replying in the current chat. Moltis supports three
    95→main outbound patterns:
    96→
    97→- **`send_message` tool** for direct proactive messages to any configured channel account/chat
    98→- **Cron job delivery** for background jobs that should post their final output to a channel
    99→- **Heartbeat delivery** for periodic heartbeat acknowledgements sent to a chosen chat
   100→
   101→Example `send_message` tool call:
   102→
   103→```json
   104→{
   105→  "account_id": "my-telegram-bot",
   106→  "to": "123456789",
   107→  "text": "Deployment finished successfully."
   108→}
   109→```
   110→
   111→`account_id` is the configured channel account name from `moltis.toml`, and
   112→`to` is the destination chat, peer, or room identifier for that platform.
   113→
   114→## Access Control
   115→
   116→All channels share the same access control model with three settings:
   117→
   118→### DM Policy
   119→
   120→Controls who can send direct messages to the bot.
   121→
   122→| Value | Behavior |
   123→|-------|----------|
   124→| `"allowlist"` | Only users listed in `allowlist` can DM (**default for all channels except WhatsApp**) |
   125→| `"open"` | Anyone can DM the bot |
   126→| `"disabled"` | DMs are silently ignored |
   127→
   128→```admonish warning title="Empty allowlist blocks everyone"
   129→When `dm_policy = "allowlist"` with an empty `allowlist`, **all DMs are blocked**.
   130→This is a security feature — removing all entries from an allowlist never silently
   131→switches to open access. Add user IDs/usernames to `allowlist` or set
   132→`dm_policy = "open"`.
   133→```
   134→
   135→### Group Policy
   136→
   137→Controls who can interact with the bot in group chats / channels / guilds.
   138→
   139→| Value | Behavior |
   140→|-------|----------|
   141→| `"open"` | Bot responds in all groups (default) |
   142→| `"allowlist"` | Only groups on the allowlist are allowed |
   143→| `"disabled"` | Group messages are silently ignored |
   144→
   145→The group allowlist field name varies by channel: `group_allowlist` (Telegram,
   146→WhatsApp, MS Teams), `guild_allowlist` (Discord), `channel_allowlist` (Slack).
   147→
   148→### Mention Mode
   149→
   150→Controls when the bot responds in groups (does not apply to DMs).
   151→
   152→| Value | Behavior |
   153→|-------|----------|
   154→| `"mention"` | Bot only responds when @mentioned (default) |
   155→| `"always"` | Bot responds to every message |
   156→| `"none"` | Bot never responds in groups (DM-only) |
   157→
   158→### Allowlist Matching
   159→
   160→All allowlist fields across all channels share the same matching behavior:
   161→
   162→- **Values are strings** — even for numeric IDs, use `"123456789"` not `123456789`
   163→- **Case-insensitive** — `"Alice"` matches `"alice"`
   164→- **Glob wildcards** — `"admin_*"`, `"*@example.com"`, `"user_*_vip"`
   165→- **Multiple identifiers** — both the user's numeric ID and username are checked (where applicable)
   166→
   167→### OTP Self-Approval
   168→
   169→Channels that support OTP (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp) allow non-allowlisted
   170→users to self-approve by entering a 6-digit code. The code appears in the web UI
   171→under **Channels > Senders**. See each channel's page for details.
   172→
   173→| Field | Default | Description |
   174→|-------|---------|-------------|
   175→| `otp_self_approval` | `true` | Enable OTP challenges for non-allowlisted DM users |
   176→| `otp_cooldown_secs` | `300` | Lockout duration after 3 failed attempts |
   177→
```

     1→# Discord
     2→
     3→Moltis can connect to Discord as a bot, letting you chat with your agent from
     4→any Discord server or DM. The integration uses Discord's
     5→[Gateway API](https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/gateway) via a
     6→persistent WebSocket connection — no public URL or webhook endpoint is required.
     7→
     8→## How It Works
     9→
    10→```
    11→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    12→│                   Discord Gateway                     │
    13→│              (wss://gateway.discord.gg)               │
    14→└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    15→                   │  persistent WebSocket
    16→                   ▼
    17→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    18→│               moltis-discord crate                    │
    19→│  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
    20→│  │  Handler   │  │  Outbound  │  │     Plugin     │  │
    21→│  │ (inbound)  │  │ (replies)  │  │  (lifecycle)   │  │
    22→│  └────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │
    23→└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
    24→                   │
    25→                   ▼
    26→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    27→│                 Moltis Gateway                        │
    28→│         (chat dispatch, tools, memory)                │
    29→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    30→```
    31→
    32→The bot connects **outward** to Discord's servers. Unlike Microsoft Teams
    33→(which requires an inbound webhook), Discord needs no port forwarding, no
    34→public domain, and no TLS certificate. This makes it especially easy to run
    35→on a home machine or behind a NAT.
    36→
    37→## Prerequisites
    38→
    39→Before configuring Moltis, create a Discord bot:
    40→
    41→1. Go to the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
    42→2. Click **New Application** and give it a name
    43→3. Navigate to **Bot** in the left sidebar
    44→4. Click **Reset Token** and copy the bot token
    45→5. Under **Privileged Gateway Intents**, enable **Message Content Intent**
    46→6. Navigate to **OAuth2 → URL Generator**
    47→   - Scopes: `bot`
    48→   - Bot Permissions: `Send Messages`, `Attach Files`, `Read Message History`, `Add Reactions`
    49→7. Copy the generated URL and open it to invite the bot to your server
    50→
    51→```admonish warning
    52→The bot token is a secret — treat it like a password. Never commit it to
    53→version control. Moltis stores it with `secrecy::Secret` and redacts it from
    54→logs, but your `moltis.toml` file is plain text on disk. Consider using
    55→[Vault](vault.md) for encryption at rest.
    56→```
    57→
    58→## Configuration
    59→
    60→Add a `[channels.discord.<account-id>]` section to your `moltis.toml`:
    61→
    62→```toml
    63→[channels.discord.my-bot]
    64→token = "MTIzNDU2Nzg5.example.bot-token"
    65→```
    66→
    67→Make sure `"discord"` is included in `channels.offered` so the Web UI shows
    68→the Discord option:
    69→
    70→```toml
    71→[channels]
    72→offered = ["telegram", "discord"]
    73→```
    74→
    75→### Configuration Fields
    76→
    77→| Field | Required | Default | Description |
    78→|-------|----------|---------|-------------|
    79→| `token` | **yes** | — | Discord bot token from the Developer Portal |
    80→| `dm_policy` | no | `"allowlist"` | Who can DM the bot: `"open"`, `"allowlist"`, or `"disabled"` |
    81→| `group_policy` | no | `"open"` | Who can talk to the bot in guild channels: `"open"`, `"allowlist"`, or `"disabled"` |
    82→| `mention_mode` | no | `"mention"` | When the bot responds in guilds: `"always"`, `"mention"` (only when @mentioned), or `"none"` |
    83→| `allowlist` | no | `[]` | Discord usernames allowed to DM the bot (when `dm_policy = "allowlist"`) |
    84→| `guild_allowlist` | no | `[]` | Guild (server) IDs allowed to interact with the bot |
    85→| `model` | no | — | Override the default model for this channel |
    86→| `model_provider` | no | — | Provider for the overridden model |
    87→| `reply_to_message` | no | `false` | Send bot responses as Discord replies to the user's message |
    88→| `ack_reaction` | no | — | Emoji reaction added while processing (e.g. `"👀"`); omit to disable |
    89→| `activity` | no | — | Bot activity status text (e.g. `"with AI"`) |
    90→| `activity_type` | no | `"custom"` | Activity type: `"playing"`, `"listening"`, `"watching"`, `"competing"`, or `"custom"` |
    91→| `status` | no | `"online"` | Bot online status: `"online"`, `"idle"`, `"dnd"`, or `"invisible"` |
    92→| `otp_self_approval` | no | `true` | Enable OTP self-approval for non-allowlisted DM users |
    93→| `otp_cooldown_secs` | no | `300` | Cooldown in seconds after 3 failed OTP attempts |
    94→
    95→### Full Example
    96→
    97→```toml
    98→[channels]
    99→offered = ["telegram", "discord"]
   100→
   101→[channels.discord.my-bot]
   102→token = "MTIzNDU2Nzg5.example.bot-token"
   103→dm_policy = "allowlist"
   104→group_policy = "open"
   105→mention_mode = "mention"
   106→allowlist = ["alice", "bob"]
   107→guild_allowlist = ["123456789012345678"]
   108→reply_to_message = true
   109→ack_reaction = "👀"
   110→model = "gpt-4o"
   111→model_provider = "openai"
   112→activity = "with AI"
   113→activity_type = "custom"
   114→status = "online"
   115→otp_self_approval = true
   116→```
   117→
   118→## Access Control
   119→
   120→Discord uses the same gating system as Telegram and Microsoft Teams:
   121→
   122→### DM Policy
   123→
   124→Controls who can send direct messages to the bot.
   125→
   126→| Value | Behavior |
   127→|-------|----------|
   128→| `"allowlist"` | Only users listed in `allowlist` can DM (default) |
   129→| `"open"` | Anyone who can reach the bot can DM it |
   130→| `"disabled"` | DMs are silently ignored |
   131→
   132→### Group Policy
   133→
   134→Controls who can interact with the bot in guild (server) channels.
   135→
   136→| Value | Behavior |
   137→|-------|----------|
   138→| `"open"` | Bot responds in any guild channel (default) |
   139→| `"allowlist"` | Only guilds listed in `guild_allowlist` are allowed |
   140→| `"disabled"` | Guild messages are silently ignored |
   141→
   142→### Mention Mode
   143→
   144→Controls when the bot responds in guild channels (does not apply to DMs).
   145→
   146→| Value | Behavior |
   147→|-------|----------|
   148→| `"mention"` | Bot only responds when @mentioned (default) |
   149→| `"always"` | Bot responds to every message in allowed channels |
   150→| `"none"` | Bot never responds in guilds (useful for DM-only bots) |
   151→
   152→### Guild Allowlist
   153→
   154→If `guild_allowlist` is non-empty, messages from guilds **not** in the list are
   155→silently dropped — regardless of `group_policy`. This provides a server-level
   156→filter on top of the channel-level policy.
   157→
   158→### OTP Self-Approval
   159→
   160→When `dm_policy = "allowlist"` and `otp_self_approval = true` (the default),
   161→unknown users who DM the bot receive a verification challenge. The flow:
   162→
   163→1. User sends a DM to the bot
   164→2. Bot responds with a challenge prompt (the 6-digit code is **not** shown to the user)
   165→3. The code appears in the Moltis web UI under **Channels → Senders**
   166→4. The bot owner shares the code with the user out-of-band
   167→5. User replies with the 6-digit code
   168→6. On success, the user is automatically added to the allowlist
   169→
   170→After 3 failed attempts, the user is locked out for `otp_cooldown_secs` seconds
   171→(default: 300). Codes expire after 5 minutes.
   172→
   173→```admonish tip
   174→This is the same OTP mechanism used by the Telegram integration. It provides a
   175→simple access control flow without requiring manual allowlist management.
   176→```
   177→
   178→## Bot Presence
   179→
   180→Configure the bot's Discord presence (the "Playing..." / "Listening to..." status)
   181→using the `activity`, `activity_type`, and `status` fields:
   182→
   183→```toml
   184→[channels.discord.my-bot]
   185→token = "..."
   186→activity = "with AI"
   187→activity_type = "custom"  # or "playing", "listening", "watching", "competing"
   188→status = "online"         # or "idle", "dnd", "invisible"
   189→```
   190→
   191→The presence is set when the bot connects to the Discord gateway. If no activity
   192→or status is configured, the bot uses Discord's default (online, no activity).
   193→
   194→## Slash Commands
   195→
   196→The bot automatically registers native Discord slash commands when it connects:
   197→
   198→| Command | Description |
   199→|---------|-------------|
   200→| `/new` | Start a new chat session |
   201→| `/clear` | Clear the current session history |
   202→| `/compact` | Summarize the current session |
   203→| `/context` | Show session info (model, tokens, plugins) |
   204→| `/model` | List or switch the AI model |
   205→| `/sessions` | List or switch chat sessions |
   206→| `/agent` | List or switch agents |
   207→| `/help` | Show available commands |
   208→
   209→Slash commands appear in Discord's command palette (type `/` in any channel where
   210→the bot is present). Responses are ephemeral — only visible to the user who
   211→invoked the command.
   212→
   213→```admonish note
   214→Text-based `/` commands (e.g. typing `/model` as a regular message) continue to
   215→work alongside native slash commands. The native commands provide autocomplete and
   216→a better Discord-native experience.
   217→```
   218→
   219→## Web UI Setup
   220→
   221→You can also configure Discord through the web interface:
   222→
   223→1. Open **Settings → Channels**
   224→2. Click **Connect Discord**
   225→3. Enter an account ID (any alias) and your bot token
   226→4. Adjust DM policy, mention mode, and allowlist as needed
   227→5. Click **Connect**
   228→
   229→The same form is available during onboarding when Discord is in `channels.offered`.
   230→
   231→## Talking to Your Bot
   232→
   233→Once the bot is connected there are several ways to interact with it.
   234→
   235→### In a Server
   236→
   237→To use the bot in a Discord server you need to invite it first:
   238→
   239→1. Go to the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
   240→2. Select your application → **OAuth2 → URL Generator**
   241→3. Scopes: check **bot**
   242→4. Bot Permissions: check **Send Messages**, **Read Message History**, and **Add Reactions**
   243→5. Copy the generated URL and open it in your browser
   244→6. Select the server you want to add the bot to and confirm
   245→
   246→```admonish tip
   247→The Moltis web UI generates this invite link automatically when you paste your
   248→bot token. Look for the "Invite bot to a server" card in the Connect Discord
   249→dialog.
   250→```
   251→
   252→Once the bot is in your server, **@mention** it in any channel to get a
   253→response (assuming `mention_mode = "mention"`, the default). If you set
   254→`mention_mode = "always"` the bot responds to every message in allowed channels.
   255→
   256→### Via Direct Message
   257→
   258→You can DM the bot directly from Discord — no shared server required:
   259→
   260→1. Open Discord and go to **Direct Messages**
   261→2. Click the **New Message** icon (or **Find or start a conversation**)
   262→3. Search for the bot's username and select it
   263→4. Send a message
   264→
   265→```admonish note
   266→If `dm_policy` is set to `"allowlist"` (the default), make sure your Discord
   267→username is listed in the `allowlist` array — otherwise the bot will ignore your
   268→DMs. Set `dm_policy = "open"` to allow anyone to DM the bot.
   269→```
   270→
   271→### Without a Shared Server
   272→
   273→DMs work even if you and the bot don't share a server. Discord bots are
   274→reachable by username from any account. This makes DMs the simplest way to
   275→start chatting — just connect the bot in Moltis and message it directly.
   276→
   277→## Message Handling
   278→
   279→### Inbound Messages
   280→
   281→When a message arrives from Discord:
   282→
   283→1. Bot's own messages are ignored
   284→2. Guild allowlist is checked (if configured)
   285→3. DM/group policy is evaluated
   286→4. Mention mode is checked (guild messages only)
   287→5. Bot mention prefix (`@BotName`) is stripped from the message text
   288→6. The message is logged and dispatched to the chat engine
   289→7. Commands (messages starting with `/`) are dispatched to the command handler
   290→
   291→### Outbound Messages
   292→
   293→Discord enforces a **2,000-character limit** per message. Moltis automatically
   294→splits long responses into multiple messages, preferring to break at newline
   295→boundaries and avoiding splits inside fenced code blocks.
   296→
   297→Streaming uses **edit-in-place** — an initial message is sent after 30 characters
   298→and then updated every 500ms as tokens arrive. If the final text exceeds 2,000
   299→characters, the first message is edited to the limit and overflow is sent as
   300→follow-up messages.
   301→
   302→### Reply-to-Message
   303→
   304→Set `reply_to_message = true` to have the bot send responses as Discord replies
   305→(threaded to the user's original message). The first chunk of a multi-chunk or
   306→streamed response carries the reply reference; follow-up chunks are sent as
   307→regular messages.
   308→
   309→### Ack Reactions
   310→
   311→Set `ack_reaction = "👀"` (or any Unicode emoji) to have the bot react to the
   312→user's message when processing starts. The reaction is removed once the response
   313→is complete. This provides a visual indicator that the bot has seen the message
   314→and is working on a reply.
   315→
   316→## Crate Structure
   317→
   318→```
   319→crates/discord/
   320→├── Cargo.toml
   321→└── src/
   322→    ├── lib.rs         # Public exports
   323→    ├── commands.rs    # Native Discord slash command registration
   324→    ├── config.rs      # DiscordAccountConfig (token, policies, presence, OTP)
   325→    ├── error.rs       # Error enum (Config, Gateway, Send, Channel)
   326→    ├── handler.rs     # serenity EventHandler (inbound + OTP + interactions)
   327→    ├── outbound.rs    # ChannelOutbound + ChannelStreamOutbound impls
   328→    ├── plugin.rs      # ChannelPlugin + ChannelStatus impls
   329→    └── state.rs       # AccountState + AccountStateMap (includes OtpState)
   330→```
   331→
   332→The crate implements the same trait set as `moltis-telegram` and `moltis-msteams`:
   333→
   334→| Trait | Purpose |
   335→|-------|---------|
   336→| `ChannelPlugin` | Start/stop accounts, lifecycle management |
   337→| `ChannelOutbound` | Send text, media, typing indicators |
   338→| `ChannelStreamOutbound` | Handle streaming responses |
   339→| `ChannelStatus` | Health probes (connected / disconnected) |
   340→
   341→## Troubleshooting
   342→
   343→### Bot doesn't respond
   344→
   345→- Verify **Message Content Intent** is enabled in the Developer Portal
   346→- Check that the bot token is correct (reset it if unsure)
   347→- Ensure the bot has been invited to the server with the right permissions
   348→- Check `dm_policy` / `group_policy` — if set to `"allowlist"`, make sure
   349→  your username or guild ID is listed
   350→- Look at logs: `RUST_LOG=moltis_discord=debug moltis`
   351→
   352→### "Gateway connection failed"
   353→
   354→- Check your network connection — the bot connects outward to
   355→  `wss://gateway.discord.gg`
   356→- Firewalls or proxies that block outbound WebSocket connections will prevent
   357→  the bot from connecting
   358→- The token may have been revoked — regenerate it in the Developer Portal
   359→
   360→### Bot responds in DMs but not in guilds
   361→
   362→- Check `mention_mode` — if set to `"mention"`, you must @mention the bot
   363→- Check `group_policy` — if `"disabled"`, guild messages are ignored
   364→- Check `guild_allowlist` — if non-empty, the guild must be listed
   365→
```

     1→// ── Shared channel RPC wrappers and validation ────────────────
     2→//
     3→// Used by page-channels.js and onboarding-view.js.
     4→
     5→import { sendRpc } from "./helpers.js";
     6→
     7→/**
     8→ * Validate required channel fields before submission.
     9→ * @param {string} type - channel type
    10→ * @param {string} accountId - account identifier
    11→ * @param {string} credential - primary credential (token or app password)
    12→ * @returns {{ valid: true } | { valid: false, error: string }}
    13→ */
    14→export function validateChannelFields(type, accountId, credential) {
    15→	if (!accountId.trim()) {
    16→		return { valid: false, error: "Account ID is required." };
    17→	}
    18→	if (!credential.trim()) {
    19→		return {
    20→			valid: false,
    21→			error: type === "msteams" ? "App password is required." : "Bot token is required.",
    22→		};
    23→	}
    24→	return { valid: true };
    25→}
    26→
    27→/**
    28→ * Add a new channel (e.g. Telegram bot).
    29→ * @param {string} type - channel type, e.g. "telegram"
    30→ * @param {string} accountId - bot username / account identifier
    31→ * @param {object} config - channel-specific config (token, dm_policy, etc.)
    32→ */
    33→export function addChannel(type, accountId, config) {
    34→	return sendRpc("channels.add", { type, account_id: accountId, config });
    35→}
    36→
    37→/**
    38→ * Fetch the current status of all configured channels.
    39→ * Resolves with the RPC response; payload has `{ channels: [] }`.
    40→ */
    41→export function fetchChannelStatus() {
    42→	return sendRpc("channels.status", {});
    43→}
    44→
    45→/**
    46→ * Default base URL for Teams webhook endpoints (current page origin).
    47→ */
    48→export function defaultTeamsBaseUrl() {
    49→	if (typeof window === "undefined") return "";
    50→	return window.location?.origin || "";
    51→}
    52→
    53→/**
    54→ * Normalise a user-provided base URL into `protocol://host`.
    55→ */
    56→export function normalizeBaseUrlForWebhook(baseUrl) {
    57→	var raw = (baseUrl || "").trim();
    58→	if (!raw) raw = defaultTeamsBaseUrl();
    59→	if (!raw) return "";
    60→	if (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(raw)) raw = `https://${raw}`;
    61→	try {
    62→		var parsed = new URL(raw);
    63→		return `${parsed.protocol}//${parsed.host}`;
    64→	} catch (_e) {
    65→		return "";
    66→	}
    67→}
    68→
    69→/**
    70→ * Generate a random 48-hex-char webhook secret.
    71→ */
    72→export function generateWebhookSecretHex() {
    73→	if (typeof window !== "undefined" && window.crypto?.getRandomValues) {
    74→		var bytes = new Uint8Array(24);
    75→		window.crypto.getRandomValues(bytes);
    76→		return Array.from(bytes, (b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
    77→	}
    78→	var value = "";
    79→	while (value.length < 48) {
    80→		value += Math.floor(Math.random() * 16).toString(16);
    81→	}
    82→	return value.slice(0, 48);
    83→}
    84→
    85→/**
    86→ * Build the full Teams messaging endpoint URL.
    87→ */
    88→export function buildTeamsEndpoint(baseUrl, accountId, webhookSecret) {
    89→	var normalizedBase = normalizeBaseUrlForWebhook(baseUrl);
    90→	var account = (accountId || "").trim();
    91→	var secret = (webhookSecret || "").trim();
    92→	if (!(normalizedBase && account && secret)) return "";
    93→	return `${normalizedBase}/api/channels/msteams/${encodeURIComponent(account)}/webhook?secret=${encodeURIComponent(secret)}`;
    94→}
    95→

  "content": "# Microsoft Teams\n\nMoltis can connect to Microsoft Teams as a bot, letting you chat with your\nagent from any Teams workspace, group chat, or direct message. The integration\nuses the [Bot Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/)\nwith an inbound webhook — your Moltis instance must be reachable from the\ninternet over HTTPS.\n\n## How It Works\n\n```\n                          Microsoft Bot Service\n                      (bot.botframework.com / Teams)\n                                    │\n                          HTTP POST (webhook)\n                                    ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                      moltis-msteams crate                     │\n│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  │\n│  │  JWT + Secret │  │  Outbound  │  │      Plugin          │  │\n│  │  Verification │  │ (replies,  │  │  (lifecycle, cards,  │  │\n│  │  (auth)       │  │  streaming)│  │   attachments)       │  │\n│  └──────────────┘  └────────────┘  └──────────────────────┘  │\n└──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘\n                           │\n                           ▼\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                     Moltis Gateway                            │\n│           (chat dispatch, tools, memory)                      │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nTeams sends each user message as an HTTP POST to your webhook endpoint.\nMoltis verifies the request (JWT signature and/or shared secret), processes\nit, and replies via the Bot Framework REST API.\n\nStreaming uses **edit-in-place** — an initial message is posted once enough\ntokens arrive, then updated at a throttled interval until the response is\ncomplete.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\nBefore configuring Moltis you need to register a bot in Azure. There are two\napproaches; the **Teams Developer Portal** route is quickest for most users.\n\n### Option A: Teams Developer Portal (recommended)\n\n1. Open the [Teams Developer Portal — Tools — Bot Management](https://dev.teams.microsoft.com/bots)\n2. Click **+ New Bot**\n3. Give the bot a name and click **Add**\n4. On the bot's page, go to **Configure** and note the **Bot ID** (this is your `app_id`)\n5. Under **Client secrets**, click **Add a client secret for your bot** and copy the generated value (this is your `app_password`)\n6. Set the **Endpoint address** to your Moltis webhook URL (see [Webhook Endpoint](#webhook-endpoint) below)\n\n### Option B: Azure Portal\n\n1. Go to the [Azure Portal — Create a resource](https://portal.azure.com/#create/Microsoft.AzureBot)\n2. Search for **Azure Bot** and click **Create**\n3. Fill in a bot handle, subscription, and resource group\n4. Under **Microsoft App ID**, select **Create new** (single-tenant is fine)\n5. Click **Create** and wait for deployment\n6. Go to the new bot resource, then **Configuration**:\n   - Copy the **Microsoft App ID** (`app_id`)\n   - Click **Manage Password** to go to **Certificates & secrets**\n   - Click **+ New client secret**, copy the value (`app_password`)\n7. Still in **Configuration**, set the **Messaging endpoint** to your Moltis webhook URL\n\n### Install the bot in Teams\n\nAfter creating the bot, you need to install it in your Teams organization:\n\n1. In the [Teams Developer Portal](https://dev.teams.microsoft.com/), go to **Apps**\n2. Click **+ New app**, give it a name, and fill in the required fields\n3. Under **App features**, click **Bot** and select your existing bot\n4. Choose the scopes: **Personal** (DMs), **Team** (channels), **Group Chat**\n5. Click **Publish** → **Publish to your org** (or use **Preview in Teams** for testing)\n6. In Teams, go to **Apps → Built for your org** and install the app\n\n```admonish warning\nThe App Password is a secret — treat it like a password. Never commit it to\nversion control. Moltis stores it with `secrecy::Secret` and redacts it from\nlogs, but your `moltis.toml` file is plain text on disk. Consider using\n[Vault](vault.md) for encryption at rest.\n```\n\n## Webhook Endpoint\n\nTeams sends messages to a webhook URL on your server. The URL pattern is:\n\n```\nhttps://<your-domain>/api/channels/msteams/<account-id>/webhook?secret=<webhook-secret>\n```\n\n- **`<your-domain>`** — your public HTTPS domain (e.g. `bot.example.com`)\n- **`<account-id>`** — the account identifier in your `moltis.toml` (e.g. `my-bot`)\n- **`<webhook-secret>`** — an optional shared secret for additional verification\n\nThe Moltis web UI and CLI both generate this URL for you. Paste it into your\nbot's **Messaging endpoint** field in the Azure Portal or Teams Developer Portal.\n\n```admonish info title=\"HTTPS required\"\nTeams requires HTTPS. For local development, use a tunnel like\n[ngrok](https://ngrok.com/) (`ngrok http 8080`) or\n[Cloudflare Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/).\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\nAdd a `[channels.msteams.<account-id>]` section to your `moltis.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[channels.msteams.my-bot]\napp_id = \"12345678-abcd-efgh-ijkl-000000000000\"\napp_password = \"your-client-secret-here\"\n```\n\n### Configuration Fields\n\n| Field | Required | Default | Description |\n|-------|----------|---------|-------------|\n| `app_id` | **yes** | — | Azure App ID (Bot ID) from the bot registration |\n| `app_password` | **yes** | — | Azure client secret for the bot |\n| `tenant_id` | no | `\"botframework.com\"` | Azure AD tenant for JWT validation. Set to your tenant ID for single-tenant bots |\n| `webhook_secret` | no | — | Shared secret appended as `?secret=...` to the webhook URL |\n| `dm_policy` | no | `\"allowlist\"` | Who can DM the bot: `\"open\"`, `\"allowlist\"`, or `\"disabled\"` |\n| `group_policy` | no | `\"open\"` | Who can talk to the bot in group chats / channels: `\"open\"`, `\"allowlist\"`, or `\"disabled\"` |\n| `mention_mode` | no | `\"mention\"` | When the bot responds in groups: `\"always\"`, `\"mention\"`, or `\"none\"` |\n| `allowlist` | no | `[]` | AAD object IDs or user IDs allowed to DM the bot |\n| `group_allowlist` | no | `[]` | Conversation/team IDs allowed for group messages |\n| `model` | no | — | Override the default model for this channel |\n| `model_provider` | no | — | Provider for the overridden model |\n| `stream_mode` | no | `\"edit_in_place\"` | `\"edit_in_place\"` (live updates) or `\"off\"` (send once complete) |\n| `edit_throttle_ms` | no | `1500` | Minimum milliseconds between streaming edits |\n| `text_chunk_limit` | no | `4000` | Maximum characters per message before splitting |\n| `reply_style` | no | `\"top_level\"` | `\"top_level\"` or `\"thread\"` (reply in thread) |\n| `welcome_card` | no | `true` | Send an Adaptive Card welcome message in DMs |\n| `group_welcome_card` | no | `false` | Send a welcome message when the bot is added to a group |\n| `bot_name` | no | `\"Moltis\"` | Display name shown on welcome cards |\n| `prompt_starters` | no | `[]` | Prompt starter buttons on the welcome card |\n| `max_retries` | no | `3` | Max retry attempts for failed sends |\n| `retry_base_delay_ms` | no | `250` | Base delay (ms) for exponential backoff |\n| `retry_max_delay_ms` | no | `10000` | Maximum retry delay (ms) |\n| `history_limit` | no | `50` | Max messages fetched for thread context (requires Graph API permissions) |\n| `graph_tenant_id` | no | — | Tenant ID for Graph API operations (thread history, reactions, search) |\n\n### Full Example\n\n```toml\n[channels]\noffered = [\"telegram\", \"msteams\", \"discord\", \"slack\"]\n\n[channels.msteams.my-bot]\napp_id = \"12345678-abcd-efgh-ijkl-000000000000\"\napp_password = \"your-client-secret-here\"\ntenant_id = \"your-azure-tenant-id\"\nwebhook_secret = \"a-long-random-secret\"\ndm_policy = \"allowlist\"\ngroup_policy = \"open\"\nmention_mode = \"mention\"\nallowlist = [\"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001\"]\nstream_mode = \"edit_in_place\"\nedit_throttle_ms = 1500\nwelcome_card = true\nbot_name = \"My Assistant\"\nprompt_starters = [\"What can you do?\", \"Help me write an email\"]\nreply_style = \"top_level\"\nmodel = \"claude-sonnet-4-20250514\"\nmodel_provider = \"anthropic\"\n```\n\n### Per-Team / Per-Channel Overrides\n\nYou can override settings for specific Teams teams or channels:\n\n```toml\n[channels.msteams.my-bot.teams.team-id-here]\nreply_style = \"thread\"\nmention_mode = \"always\"\n\n[channels.msteams.my-bot.teams.team-id-here.channels.general-channel-id]\nmodel = \"gpt-4o\"\nmodel_provider = \"openai\"\nmention_mode = \"mention\"\n```\n\n## Access Control\n\nTeams uses the same gating system as other channels:\n\n### DM Policy\n\nControls who can send direct messages to the bot.\n\n| Value | Behavior |\n|-------|----------|\n| `\"allowlist\"` | Only users listed in `allowlist` can DM (default) |\n| `\"open\"` | Anyone who can reach the bot can DM it |\n| `\"disabled\"` | DMs are silently ignored |\n\n### Group Policy\n\nControls who can interact with the bot in group chats and team channels.\n\n| Value | Behavior |\n|-------|----------|\n| `\"open\"` | Bot responds in any group chat (default) |\n| `\"allowlist\"` | Only conversations listed in `group_allowlist` are allowed |\n| `\"disabled\"` | Group messages are silently ignored |\n\n### Mention Mode\n\nControls when the bot responds in group chats (does not apply to DMs).\n\n| Value | Behavior |\n|-------|----------|\n| `\"mention\"` | Bot only responds when @mentioned (default) |\n| `\"always\"` | Bot responds to every message in allowed groups |\n| `\"none\"` | Bot never responds in groups (DM-only) |\n\n### Finding User IDs\n\nTo add users to the allowlist, you need their **AAD Object ID**. You can find\nthis in:\n\n- **Azure Portal** → Azure Active Directory → Users → select user → Object ID\n- **Microsoft 365 Admin Center** → Users → Active users → select user → Properties\n- **Teams Admin Center** → Users → select user\n\nAlternatively, set `dm_policy = \"open\"` initially and check the Moltis web UI\nunder **Channels → Senders** to see user IDs as messages arrive.\n\n## Streaming\n\nBy default, Teams uses **edit-in-place** streaming:\n\n1. After ~20 characters accumulate, an initial message is posted with \"...\"\n2. Every 1.5 seconds (configurable via `edit_throttle_ms`), the message is\n   edited with the latest accumulated text\n3. When the response is complete, a final edit removes the \"...\" suffix\n\nSet `stream_mode = \"off\"` to disable streaming and send the complete response\nas a single message.\n\n```toml\n[channels.msteams.my-bot]\nstream_mode = \"edit_in_place\"\nedit_throttle_ms = 1500\n```\n\n## Welcome Cards\n\nWhen a user first messages the bot in a DM, Moltis sends an\n[Adaptive Card](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/adaptive-cards/) with a\ngreeting and optional prompt starter buttons:\n\n```toml\n[channels.msteams.my-bot]\nwelcome_card = true\nbot_name = \"My Assistant\"\nprompt_starters = [\"What can you do?\", \"Help me write an email\", \"Summarize this document\"]\n```\n\nSet `welcome_card = false` to disable. Set `group_welcome_card = true` to also\nsend a text welcome when the bot is added to a group chat.\n\n## Interactive Messages\n\nThe bot supports Adaptive Cards for interactive button menus. When an agent\nreturns an interactive message (buttons), Moltis renders it as an Adaptive\nCard with `Action.Submit` buttons. Clicking a button sends the callback data\nback to the bot as a regular message.\n\n## Attachments\n\n### Inbound\n\nWhen users send images or files in Teams, Moltis downloads the attachments\nusing the bot's access token and passes them to the LLM as multimodal content\n(if the model supports it).\n\n### Outbound\n\n- **Images in DMs**: sent inline as base64 data URLs\n- **External URLs**: sent as Bot Framework URL attachments\n- **Large files**: currently not supported (requires SharePoint/OneDrive integration)\n\n## Thread Context (Graph API)\n\nWith Graph API permissions, the bot can read conversation history for\nmulti-turn context in group chats. This requires:\n\n1. An **app registration** with `Chat.Read.All` or `ChannelMessage.Read.All`\n   permissions (application-level, not delegated)\n2. **Admin consent** for these permissions in your Azure AD tenant\n3. Set `graph_tenant_id` in the config\n\n```toml\n[channels.msteams.my-bot]\ngraph_tenant_id = \"your-azure-tenant-id\"\nhistory_limit = 50\n```\n\n## Reactions\n\nThe bot supports adding and removing reactions (like, heart, laugh, surprised,\nsad, angry) via the Graph API beta endpoints. This requires the same Graph API\npermissions as thread context.\n\n## Web UI Setup\n\nYou can configure Teams through the web interface:\n\n1. Open **Settings → Channels**\n2. Click **Connect Microsoft Teams**\n3. Enter your **App ID** and **App Password** from the Azure bot registration\n4. Optionally enter a **Webhook Secret** (one is generated if left blank)\n5. Set the **Public Base URL** to your Moltis server's HTTPS URL\n6. Click **Bootstrap Teams** to generate the messaging endpoint\n7. Click **Copy Endpoint** and paste it into your bot's Messaging Endpoint in the Azure Portal or Teams Developer Portal\n8. Adjust DM policy, mention mode, and allowlist as needed\n9. Click **Connect Microsoft Teams**\n\nThe same form is available during onboarding when `\"msteams\"` is in\n`channels.offered`.\n\n## CLI Setup\n\nUse the CLI bootstrap command for a quick setup:\n\n```bash\nmoltis channels teams bootstrap \\\n  --account-id my-bot \\\n  --app-id 12345678-abcd-efgh-ijkl-000000000000 \\\n  --app-password your-client-secret \\\n  --base-url https://bot.example.com\n```\n\nThis generates the webhook endpoint URL and writes the configuration to\n`moltis.toml`. Add `--dry-run` to preview without saving, or `--open` to\nlaunch the Azure documentation in your browser.\n\n## Crate Structure\n\n```\ncrates/msteams/\n├── Cargo.toml\n└── src/\n    ├── lib.rs                       # Public exports\n    ├── activity.rs                  # Teams activity model & parsing\n    ├── attachments.rs               # Inbound download + outbound media\n    ├── auth.rs                      # OAuth2 token acquisition + caching\n    ├── cards.rs                     # Adaptive Card builders (welcome, polls)\n    ├── channel_webhook_verifier.rs  # Shared-secret webhook verification\n    ├── chunking.rs                  # Message text chunking\n    ├── config.rs                    # MsTeamsAccountConfig + per-team overrides\n    ├── errors.rs                    # Error classification + retry logic\n    ├── graph.rs                     # Graph API (history, reactions, search, pins)\n    ├── jwt.rs                       # Bot Framework JWT validation (JWKS)\n    ├── outbound.rs                  # ChannelOutbound + streaming + reactions\n    ├── plugin.rs                    # ChannelPlugin + ChannelThreadContext\n    ├── state.rs                     # AccountState + JWT validator\n    └── streaming.rs                 # Edit-in-place streaming session\n```\n\nThe crate implements the same trait set as other channel crates:\n\n| Trait | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `ChannelPlugin` | Start/stop accounts, lifecycle management |\n| `ChannelOutbound` | Send text, media, cards, typing indicators, reactions |\n| `ChannelStreamOutbound` | Handle streaming responses (edit-in-place) |\n| `ChannelStatus` | Health probes (connected / waiting for first activity) |\n| `ChannelThreadContext` | Fetch conversation history via Graph API |\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Bot doesn't respond\n\n- Verify the **Messaging endpoint** in the Azure Portal matches your Moltis webhook URL\n- Check that `app_id` and `app_password` are correct\n- Ensure your server is reachable from the internet over HTTPS\n- Check `dm_policy` — if set to `\"allowlist\"`, make sure your user ID is listed\n- Check `mention_mode` — in group chats, you may need to @mention the bot\n- Look at logs: `RUST_LOG=moltis_msteams=debug moltis`\n\n### \"Teams token acquisition failed\"\n\n- The `app_password` may have expired — rotate the client secret in the Azure Portal\n- Check that `oauth_tenant` and `oauth_scope` are correct (defaults should work for most setups)\n- Network issues: Moltis must be able to reach `login.microsoftonline.com`\n\n### Webhook returns 401 / 403\n\n- If using JWT validation: check that `tenant_id` matches your Azure AD tenant\n- If using shared secret: check that the `?secret=...` in the webhook URL matches `webhook_secret` in the config\n- The JWKS endpoint (`login.botframework.com`) must be reachable for JWT validation\n\n### Bot responds in DMs but not in groups\n\n- Check `mention_mode` — if set to `\"mention\"`, you must @mention the bot\n- Check `group_policy` — if `\"disabled\"`, group messages are ignored\n- Check `group_allowlist` — if non-empty, the group/team must be listed\n\n### Messages are duplicated\n\n- Moltis returns `202 Accepted` immediately to prevent Teams retry timeouts.\n  If you see duplicates, check for multiple Moltis instances pointing at the\n  same webhook URL, or verify the deduplication middleware is working\n  (duplicate activity IDs are filtered automatically)\n\n### Streaming doesn't work\n\n- Set `stream_mode = \"edit_in_place\"` (the default)\n- Streaming requires the bot to have permission to update activities\n- Some Teams clients (older mobile versions) may not render edits in real time\n"
}

## Changes Made

### New Documentation

**`docs/src/teams.md`** — Full Microsoft Teams setup guide (~300 lines) following the same structure as Discord/Telegram/Slack guides:

  - **Option A: Teams Developer Portal** (recommended, easiest) — links to `dev.teams.microsoft.com/bots`, explains Bot Management, client secrets
  - **Option B: Azure Portal** — links to `portal.azure.com/#create/Microsoft.AzureBot`, explains Azure Bot resource creation
  - **Install the bot in Teams** — how to create a Teams App, add bot features, publish to your org
- **Webhook Endpoint** — URL pattern explained, HTTPS requirement, tunnel suggestions (ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel)
- **Configuration** — minimal example + full reference table of all 25 config fields with defaults
- **Full Example** — complete TOML snippet with common options
- **Per-Team/Per-Channel Overrides** — TOML example for nested team/channel configs
- **Access Control** — DM Policy, Group Policy, Mention Mode tables + how to find user AAD Object IDs
- **Streaming** — edit-in-place explanation with config options

## Microsoft Teams Integration Audit Report

I've completed a thorough audit of the Microsoft Teams integration across the codebase. Here are the findings:

### 1. CLI Bootstrap Command (`crates/cli/src/channel_commands.rs`)

**Status: MOSTLY COMPLETE BUT MISSING FIELDS**

The bootstrap command supports:
- ✅ App ID and App Password (core credentials)
- ✅ Webhook secret generation with custom values
- ✅ OAuth tenant/scope configuration
- ✅ DM/group policies and mention modes
- ✅ Allowlists (preserved from existing configs)
- ✅ Model selection
- ✅ Links to both Teams Developer Portal and Azure Portal

**Missing fields NOT handled by bootstrap (but ARE documented in template):**
- ❌ `tenant_id` - NOT in CLI args (defaults to "botframework.com" in config.rs)
- ❌ `stream_mode` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `reply_style` - NOT set by bootstrap  
- ❌ `text_chunk_limit` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `welcome_card` / `group_welcome_card` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `bot_name` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `prompt_starters` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `edit_throttle_ms` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `max_retries` / `retry_base_delay_ms` / `retry_max_delay_ms` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `graph_tenant_id` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ `history_limit` - NOT set by bootstrap
- ❌ Per-team/per-channel overrides (`teams` map) - NOT set by bootstrap

The bootstrap code intentionally preserves existing values for these fields using `map.remove()`, so if you run bootstrap again on an existing account, the new fields are retained.

### 2. Locale Files (JS Internationalization)

**Status: INCOMPLETE - HARDCODED STRINGS IN ENGLISH ONLY**

The locale files (`crates/web/src/assets/js/locales/{fr,zh}/channels.js`) contain **NO Teams-specific strings at all** - they're Telegram-only:
- `addTelegramBot`
- `botFather`
- `botToken`
- `telegramBotTutorial`
- etc.

Hardcoded strings in `page-channels.js` that should be localizable:
- ❌ "Microsoft Teams" (line 57)
- ❌ "Connect Telegram" modal title (line 464) - generic but needs Teams variant
- ❌ "Connect Microsoft Teams" (line 595)
- ❌ "Teams endpoint generated" toast (line 536)
- ❌ All Teams setup instructions in AddTeamsModal (lines 598-657):
  - "How to create a Teams bot"
  - "Option A: Teams Developer Portal (easiest)"
  - "Option B: Azure Portal"
  - "Bot ID", "Client secrets", etc.
  - "Full guide" link

**Missing translations:** French and Chinese versions have ZERO Teams content.

### 3. ConnectionModeHint Component (`page-channels.js`)

**Status: GENERIC BUT ADEQUATE**

The `ConnectionModeHint` component correctly displays the webhook hint for Teams:
- ✅ Shows "Webhook" label with "Requires a publicly reachable URL" message
- ✅ Not Teams-specific but appropriate for webhook-mode channels
- ⚠️ Could be enhanced with Teams-specific guidance (e.g., "Microsoft Teams requires HTTPS and a public endpoint")

### 4. Edit Channel Modal (`page-channels.js` lines 1091-1240)

**Status: LIMITED EDITING CAPABILITY**

Edit modal for Teams allows:
- ✅ Update App Password
- ✅ Update Webhook Secret
- ✅ DM Policy
- ✅ Group Mention Mode
- ✅ Default Model

**Missing fields - NOT editable:**
- ❌ `stream_mode`
- ❌ `reply_style`
- ❌ `text_chunk_limit`
- ❌ `welcome_card` / `group_welcome_card`
- ❌ `bot_name`
- ❌ `prompt_starters`
- ❌ `edit_throttle_ms`
- ❌ `max_retries` / retry configs
- ❌ `graph_tenant_id`
- ❌ `history_limit`
- ❌ Per-team/per-channel overrides

Users cannot adjust streaming, welcome card behavior, text chunking, or retry settings through the Web UI - they must edit `moltis.toml` directly.

### 5. GON Data (Server-Injected Data)

**Status: UNCLEAR**

Could not locate explicit `build_gon_data()` function or `channel_descriptors` injection in `crates/gateway/src/server.rs`. The code references Teams but the gon data builder isn't visible in the searched sections. The web UI uses `getGon("channel_descriptors")` to get capability info, which appears to work (descriptors are displayed correctly).

### 6. Health Probe Output (`crates/msteams/src/plugin.rs`)

**Status: MINIMAL BUT FUNCTIONAL**

The health probe returns:
- ✅ Connected status
- ✅ Account ID
- ✅ Details: "waiting for first inbound activity" or "known conversations: N"

**Limitations:**
- Returns only conversation count, not webhook verification status
- No indication of authentication errors
- No credential validation in the probe itself

### 7. E2E Test Coverage (`crates/web/ui/e2e/specs/`)

**Status: NOT FOUND**

- ❌ **No Teams channel setup tests** in Playwright e2e specs
- ❌ No test for "Connect Microsoft Teams" modal
- ❌ No test for Teams bootstrap endpoint generation
- ❌ No test for Teams webhook configuration validation
- Compare: Other channels (Discord, Slack, WhatsApp) also lack dedicated e2e tests

All other channels are similarly untested in e2e.

### 8. Config Validation (`crates/config/src/validate.rs`)

**Status: MINIMAL**

- ✅ Basic schema validation for msteams channel exists (line 411: `("msteams", Map(Box::new(Leaf)))`)
- ⚠️ No semantic validation for Teams-specific fields
- ⚠️ No validation of `tenant_id` format
- ⚠️ No validation that `graph_tenant_id` (if provided) matches expectations
- ⚠️ No warnings for unconfigured optional fields like `bot_name` or `graph_tenant_id`

### 9. Redacted Config (`crates/msteams/src/config.rs`)

**Status: INCOMPLETE**

The `RedactedConfig` serializer omits:
- ✅ Secrets (`app_password`, `webhook_secret`)
- ✅ Basic fields (policies, mention mode, allowlists)
- ✅ Streaming fields (`stream_mode`, `reply_style`, `edit_throttle_ms`, `text_chunk_limit`, `welcome_card`)

**But misses:**
- ❌ `bot_name`, `prompt_starters`, `group_welcome_card`
- ❌ `max_retries`, `retry_base_delay_ms`, `retry_max_delay_ms`
- ❌ `graph_tenant_id`, `history_limit`
- ❌ `teams` (per-team/per-channel overrides)

The field count hardcoded at line 210 (`count = 9`) is inaccurate for what's actually serialized. This will cause serialization failures if optional fields are present.

### 10. Documentation in Config Template

**Status: COMPREHENSIVE**

The config template (`crates/config/src/template.rs`) documents ALL Teams fields including:
- ✅ New streaming fields
- ✅ Welcome cards
- ✅ Retry configuration
- ✅ Graph API settings
- ✅ Per-team/per-channel overrides

This is accurate and complete.

## Summary of Issues Needing Attention

### High Priority
1. **Redacted Config field count bug** - The hardcoded field count (9) at line 210 of `config.rs` doesn't match the serialized fields and will cause runtime serialization errors
2. **Edit modal is incomplete** - Users cannot adjust streaming, welcome cards, text chunking, or retry settings through the Web UI
3. **CLI bootstrap doesn't support `tenant_id`** - Users with non-default tenants must manually edit config files

### Medium Priority  
1. **No localization** - Teams strings are hardcoded in English only (French and Chinese translations missing)
2. **No E2E tests** - Teams channel setup has zero Playwright test coverage
3. **Health probe is minimal** - Doesn't validate credentials or webhook configuration

### Low Priority
1. **ConnectionModeHint generic** - Could mention Teams-specific requirements (HTTPS, public endpoint)
2. **Config validation is basic** - No semantic validation of Teams-specific fields

   207→fn required_value(
   208→    provided: Option<String>,
   209→    prompt: &str,
   210→    placeholder: Option<&str>,
   211→) -> Result<String> {
   212→    match provided {
   213→        Some(value) if !value.trim().is_empty() => Ok(value.trim().to_string()),
   214→        _ => prompt_required(prompt, placeholder),
   215→    }
   216→}
   217→
   218→fn prompt_required(prompt: &str, default: Option<&str>) -> Result<String> {
   219→    let mut stdout = std::io::stdout();
   220→    match default {
   221→        Some(value) if !value.trim().is_empty() => write!(stdout, "{prompt} [{value}]: ")?,
   222→        _ => write!(stdout, "{prompt}: ")?,
   223→    }
   224→    stdout.flush()?;
   225→
   226→    let mut line = String::new();
   227→    std::io::stdin().read_line(&mut line)?;
   228→    let trimmed = line.trim();
   229→    if trimmed.is_empty() {
   230→        return default
   231→            .map(|value| value.trim().to_string())
   232→            .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
   233→            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("{prompt} is required"));
   234→    }

   238→fn prompt_yes_no(prompt: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
   239→    loop {
   240→        let default = if default_yes {
   241→            "y"
   242→        } else {
   243→            "n"
   244→        };
   245→        let answer = prompt_required(
   246→            &format!(
   247→                "{prompt} [{}]",
   248→                if default_yes {
   249→                    "Y/n"
   250→                } else {
   251→                    "y/N"
   252→                }
   253→            ),
   254→            Some(default),
   255→        )?;
   256→        match answer.trim().to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
   257→            "y" | "yes" => return Ok(true),
   258→            "n" | "no" => return Ok(false),
   259→            _ => println!("Please answer with 'y' or 'n'."),
   260→        }
   261→    }
   262→}

   264→fn build_channel_config(
   265→    app_id: &str,
   266→    app_password: &str,
   267→    oauth_tenant: &str,
   268→    oauth_scope: &str,
   269→    webhook_secret: &str,
   270→    existing: Option<&Value>,
   271→) -> Value {
   272→    let mut map: Map<String, Value> = existing
   273→        .and_then(Value::as_object)
   274→        .cloned()
   275→        .unwrap_or_default();
   276→
   277→    map.insert("app_id".into(), Value::String(app_id.to_string()));
   278→    map.insert(
   279→        "app_password".into(),
   280→        Value::String(app_password.to_string()),
   281→    );
   282→    map.insert(
   283→        "oauth_tenant".into(),
   284→        Value::String(oauth_tenant.to_string()),
   285→    );
   286→    map.insert("oauth_scope".into(), Value::String(oauth_scope.to_string()));
   287→    let dm_policy = map
   288→        .remove("dm_policy")
   289→        .unwrap_or_else(|| Value::String("allowlist".into()));
   290→    let group_policy = map
   291→        .remove("group_policy")
   292→        .unwrap_or_else(|| Value::String("open".into()));
   293→    let mention_mode = map
   294→        .remove("mention_mode")
   295→        .unwrap_or_else(|| Value::String("mention".into()));
   296→    let allowlist = map
   297→        .remove("allowlist")
   298→        .unwrap_or_else(|| Value::Array(Vec::new()));
   299→    let group_allowlist = map
   300→        .remove("group_allowlist")
   301→        .unwrap_or_else(|| Value::Array(Vec::new()));
   302→
   303→    map.insert("dm_policy".into(), dm_policy);
   304→    map.insert("group_policy".into(), group_policy);
   305→    map.insert("mention_mode".into(), mention_mode);
   306→    map.insert("allowlist".into(), allowlist);
   307→    map.insert("group_allowlist".into(), group_allowlist);
   308→
   309→    if webhook_secret.trim().is_empty() {
   310→        map.remove("webhook_secret");
   311→    } else {
   312→        map.insert(
   313→            "webhook_secret".into(),
   314→            Value::String(webhook_secret.to_string()),
   315→        );
   316→    }
   317→
   318→    Value::Object(map)
   319→}

   321→fn default_gateway_base_url(config: &moltis_config::MoltisConfig) -> String {
   322→    let scheme = if config.tls.enabled {
   323→        "https"
   324→    } else {
   325→        "http"
   326→    };
   327→    let host = match config.server.bind.as_str() {
   328→        "0.0.0.0" | "::" | "[::]" => "localhost",
   329→        other => other,
   330→    };
   331→    format!("{scheme}://{host}:{}", config.server.port)
   332→}
